title: VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns
subtopics: Limitations compared with modern object-oriented languages
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of vbscript classes and object-oriented patterns in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: Introduction to VBScript classes and Class definitions.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study vbscript classes and object-oriented patterns as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 30 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Intermediate VBScript code benefits from predictable object lifetime, focused error handling, and small reusable procedures. For 'VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns', choose the simplest construct that matches the requirement, document any COM dependency, and avoid suppressing errors across unrelated statements. A legacy script can be improved without changing externally visible behavior by adding focused checks first.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: Introduction to VBScript classes; Class definitions; Properties and methods; The Class_Initialize event; Object creation and lifetime; Organizing reusable logic into classes; Limitations compared with modern object-oriented languages. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: VBScript Classes and Object-Oriented Patterns
content_blocks.code:
<%
Class Greeting
  Public Function Message(name)
    Message = "Hello, " & CStr(name)
  End Function
End Class
Dim greeting
Set greeting = New Greeting
Response.Write Server.HTMLEncode(greeting.Message("Ada"))
Set greeting = Nothing
%>
content_blocks.run_instructions: VBScript classes are limited compared with modern OOP systems. Test the exact target engine and keep COM and class dependencies documented. The standard CodeLeaf browser playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only; it does not execute Classic ASP, VBScript, ADO, IIS commands, PowerShell, or SQL. This block is therefore marked for static inspection unless you run it in the clearly identified local tool.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original sample and test data. Change one condition, input, provider setting, or runtime option at a time, then compare observed behavior with the expected result.
content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use a local Classic ASP page. Change one value or statement at a time, capture the observed output, and check at least one empty, malformed, or boundary value. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of vbscript classes and object-oriented patterns. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small, reviewable demonstration of vbscript classes and object-oriented patterns using synthetic data. Include at least one of these syllabus concepts: Introduction to VBScript classes. State the expected result first, then add one invalid or boundary case and explain how your program should behave.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.

common_mistakes.why: Query strings, form fields, cookies, and hidden controls remain client-controlled.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and apply authorization and output encoding at the appropriate boundary.
